# Threetopia

> Creator platform for reusable Three.js assets and fixed-tile world packages. The public shared world is currently a map preview, not a released playable world.

A world package requires a tile selected and reserved BEFORE creation. Any free coordinate sharing an edge with a published tile is available; there is no ring-filling requirement. Reservations do not open neighbors until published. Threetopia owns the immutable host tile. Read the per-coordinate choices from /api/tiles: layout and rotation must match neighbors. Version 4 build areas and content origin vary by layout; never assume a universal circular slot or a single floor height. Tidewater declares requiredOpenWater in its source metadata: cells (1,1) and (2,0) are protected whale habitat, cannot be reserved or built on, and must stay connected through unoccupied water to the exterior ocean. Protected cells provide no build rights even when an older reservation exists. Preserve Tidewater’s protected harbor approach to exterior ocean; dry tiles, isolated ponds and enclosed holes do not satisfy it. The registry checks reservations and publications. Use CLI 0.7.1 or later for complete scenes and managed namespaces. Every world requires detailed world content, simplified map content and overview content. CLI and server enforce actual geometry, budgets, tile ownership and the canonical contract. Authenticate through email and browser-approved CLI login. Do not invent package names or assume npm publication.

## Convert an existing scene — propose reusable packages
- Plan one world-tile composition, one separate map-tile package (`map` and `overview` exports), and reusable system packages beneath both. Compositions must consume the extracted implementations through declared dependencies; wrapping the whole demo in one bundle does not satisfy this package plan. Verify installation and rebuild without access to the original source tree.
- A conversion covers the entire requested scene: visuals, shaders, simulation, gameplay, animation, audio, UI and every asset. Do not finish with selected components or silently substitute static approximations. Inventory and map every feature, preserve the original source revision, and verify behavior before claiming completion.
- [Complete playable scene packages](https://docs.threetopia.com/scenes.md): preserve the full runtime with `iframe-scene-v1`; use simplified GLBs separately for map representations. CLI 0.7.1+ previews and installs both.
- Begin with the creator's source repository; an X video is not sufficient source code.
- Run `threetopia analyze PATH --json` (CLI 0.6.0+) without executing source. Review diagnostics, dependency closures and host coupling. An incomplete scan is not a full assessment.
- Search the real asset catalog below, then propose cohesive new packages with source evidence, configurable APIs, dependencies, provenance and visual/runtime tradeoffs. Do not split every mesh into a package or invent published names.
- Ask before rewriting source unless the creator has already authorized the extraction. Existing approval covers routine implementation steps; do not ask repeatedly.
- Keep the original scene consuming the extracted components and demonstrate them in a second independent scene. Test isolated instances, host-owned time and idempotent cleanup.
- Run `threetopia check --json`, component tests and browser/visual checks. Static validation does not prove behavior or appearance.
- Every package needs a specific README with real code, dependencies and cleanup; world/map README examples must show their subpackage composition. Supply previews with relevant settings and label contextual demos clearly. Preserve requested author scopes; `threetopia namespaces` lists the scopes an account may manage.
- Preserve licenses and source credits. Reserve a real tile before world creation. Push privately for review; publish only when release is requested.
- [Agent conversion workflow](https://docs.threetopia.com/conversion.md): analysis, package proposals, refactoring, local checks and registration with `create --from`.
- [Complete Tidewater conversion](https://docs.threetopia.com/tidewater.md): one world-tile, one map-tile and 18 sub-packages; all 130 source files and original assets accounted for, installed dependency rebuild and GPU behavior tests. Published as `@dgreenheck/tidewater-*` version 0.1.0, temporarily managed by `@promontis`; each package has its own README, composition examples and preview settings.

## Reusable packages — consult before generating assets
- [Package installation and reuse](https://docs.threetopia.com/packages.md): exact versions, exports, dependency locks, recorded installations.
- [Live reusable asset catalog](https://creators.threetopia.com/api/packages?kind=asset): search real published packages by name, description, creator and tags; combine kind/category/creator/license/tag filters. Follow page/perPage and the returned pages count; never guess names. See the API reference for exact parameters.
- [Original Threetopia beacon](https://creators.threetopia.com/api/resolve?name=%40threetopia%2Fbeacon&version=1.0.0): MIT example with map and world exports.
- [Creator package browser](https://creators.threetopia.com/packages)

## Contracts and tools
- [Package JSON schema](https://docs.threetopia.com/schema/package.json)
- [Current tile positions and compatible Wang layouts and rotations](https://creators.threetopia.com/api/tiles)
- [Standalone CLI v0.7.1](https://docs.threetopia.com/downloads/threetopia-cli-0.7.1.tgz): install with npm install -g URL; not yet on npm registry.
- [SDK v0.7.1](https://docs.threetopia.com/downloads/threetopia-sdk-0.7.1.tgz): versioned authored and generated Wang hosts, neighbor matching, locked build areas and geometry validation.
- [Full documentation](https://docs.threetopia.com/llms-full.txt)
